callChainInspected.finding: SDK adapter stages/backfills, runs managed cron and observes publishers before stopping; does not implement native scope ownership.
Detached job is queued with queueMicrotask and returns pending; this boundary does not exit async-work ownership.
Native generator invokes completion and catches errors into fallback Diary publication.
Real completion awaits execution preparation and authorization before background enqueue; omitted by the fixture adapter.
Native plugin completion uses the background lane before isolated completion.
Queue captures and later restores the ambient async context, including work ownership; it does not by itself register work in that scope.
Execution.run leaves operator tool authority, not the async-work scope. No authorization bypass was tested.
Actual budget-confounded rejection stack reaches this completion route.
Isolated completion enters resource ownership before its completion body.
Resource wrapper captures then tracks the ambient owner before running the body.
Closed owner rejects with the exact observed error; closing owner still accepts track.
Generation creates a work scope; selected owner identity comes from the retained trace, not this static first match.
runGeneration cleanup drains owned work; queue membership alone does not make an unregistered Diary job pending in that owner.

interpretation.demonstrated: The real native detached Diary and resource wrapper can produce the exact closed-owner error without a budget denial. The real background queue retains the closed owner. With identical completion payloads, changing registration/drain order changes the result.
notDemonstrated: The original uninstrumented failure followed this exact order.

A supported SDK fix is required or has been implemented.

Full Gateway authorization, embedded generation and provider cancellation were executed by the offline experiment.
interpretation.controls: Open owner, closing-but-not-closed owner with pending work, registration before drain, awaited non-detached Diary and no ambient owner all published fixture text in three repeats per route. The closing controls ignore provider cancellation and prove only scope admission behavior.

stoppingRationale: New offline native tests now establish a concrete ownership mechanism without spending tokens.

Historical healthy matched native/SDK work already passed; another unmodified paid repeat could add a sample but would not reconstruct the original missing ownership stack or demonstrate a route-specific defect.
Forcing delays or changing ownership in a live run would test an induced trigger, already isolated offline, not repair the original verdict.
No supported SDK correction follows from this evidence. Changing native detachment, cancellation or drain policy would cross the no-fork boundary.

The next causal evidence needed is an unmodified full native rejection with owner creation, registration and cleanup timing plus matched SDK/direct inputs. That remains unresolved; useful future investigation is not claimed exhausted.
